title: Sea Gate to the Unmarked Tomb: the Moneyman, the Islands, and the Agreement
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Brooklyn, the birth at the edge of the borough
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the birthplace is attested only as Brooklyn, and the pool's Coney Island Hospital detail is dropped as unsupported
stops.campa: Jeffrey Edward Epstein is born in Brooklyn on the twentieth of January, second son of Pauline Stolofsky and Seymour George Epstein, a groundskeeper for the city parks department. The borough in 1953 is boardwalks and shipyards, and the family is neither poor nor comfortable. The record of the day is a certificate with a weight and a time on it, filed in a borough office no reporter will think to open for another forty-six years. The certificate names the borough and no hospital. Later accounts supply one anyway, and none of them cites the record.
suggested_refs: Brooklyn birth records, January 1953; the borough's postwar housing stock along Coney Island

stops.name: Sea Gate, the gated strip at the end of the island
stops.date_confidence: inferred; the family's residence in Sea Gate is attested across the childhood years, the specific year is not
stops.campa: The family lives in Sea Gate, the gated strip at the western tip of Coney Island where the beach turns into the harbor. His father tends the borough's parks and his mother keeps the house. The boy is quick with numbers and short on warmth, a chess player rather than a ball player, and he tells associates decades later that the neighborhood taught him nothing he wanted to keep. The gate still stands. The house where he sleeps as a teenager is one shingled box among many, and no marker distinguishes it from its neighbors.
sources: Vicky Ward, 'The Talented Mr. Epstein', Vanity Fair, March 2003
suggested_refs: The Sea Gate Association gatehouse; Public School 188 and Mark Twain Junior High, Coney Island

stops.name: Lafayette High School, the graduation at sixteen
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; month set to the ordinary June commencement, day defaulted
stops.campa: He graduates from Lafayette High School on Benson Avenue in Bath Beach at sixteen, two years early, having skipped grades on the strength of his mathematics. Lafayette is a large public school better known for producing ballplayers than financiers, and he leaves nothing in its yearbooks but a name and a date. He enters advanced coursework that autumn and never completes a degree in anything, at Cooper Union or anywhere after it. The school still stands on Benson Avenue and still teaches Brooklyn's children.
sources: Miami Herald, 'Perversion of Justice' (Julie K. Brown, 2018)
suggested_refs: Lafayette High School, 2630 Benson Avenue, Bath Beach; its 1969 yearbook

stops.name: Cooper Union, the courses without matriculation
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; attendance 1969-1971 rests on the institution's 2019 public statements, not on any produced registrar record
stops.campa: He takes advanced mathematics at Cooper Union on Astor Place, where tuition is free and the coursework outruns anything Lafayette offered. He earns no degree here. Cooper Union's own statements in 2019 say he was never a fully matriculated student, and the two years survive in the institution's account rather than in any diploma. No registrar record has been produced by anyone since. He can do the mathematics and he cannot document it, and five years from now the Dalton School hires him to teach it without asking.
suggested_refs: The Cooper Union Foundation Building, Astor Place; the tuition-free model that drew him

stops.name: The Courant Institute, mathematical physiology
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month; enrolled September 1971 to June 1974
stops.campa: He enrolls at New York University's Courant Institute on Mercer Street and studies mathematical physiology until June 1974, leaving without a degree. Colleagues in later decades describe a man who talks options pricing and probability with real fluency, the training having taken even where the credential did not. Earlier accounts of these three years call the field physics; it was physiology. He leaves Washington Square at twenty-one holding no qualification of any kind, and funds laboratories at Harvard and MIT before he is fifty.
suggested_refs: The Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences, 251 Mercer Street

stops.name: The Dalton School, hired by Donald Barr
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month of hire; the dismissal in early 1976 is attested to the year
stops.campa: Twenty-one years old and holding no bachelor's degree, he is hired to teach calculus and mathematics at the Dalton School on East 89th Street, among the most expensive private schools in Manhattan. The headmaster who hires him is Donald Barr. Students find him unlike their other teachers, younger and more interested, and he is dismissed in early 1976 for poor performance. Dalton never asks to see a transcript in the two years he works there, and neither does the Wall Street firm that takes him next.
suggested_refs: The Dalton School, 108 East 89th Street; Donald Barr's tenure as headmaster

stops.name: Bear Stearns, the junior assistant
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; the firm's Manhattan pin is generic, since Bear Stearns did not occupy 245 Park Avenue until 1987
stops.campa: A Dalton father recommends him by telephone to Alan Greenberg at Bear Stearns, and the mathematics teacher without a degree walks onto a Wall Street trading floor as a low-level junior assistant. He is twenty-three. He learns options, tax structure, and the particular arithmetic of very large private fortunes, and he learns which men have them. The firm is not yet at 245 Park Avenue and will not be until 1987, six years after he is gone. He works here five years, and never draws a salary from anyone else for the rest of his life.
suggested_refs: Bear Stearns under Alan Greenberg in the late 1970s; the options desk of that era

stops.name: Bear Stearns, limited partner at twenty-seven
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year for the partnership; the Cosmopolitan feature is attested to July 1980
stops.campa: At twenty-seven he is made a limited partner on a salary of two hundred thousand dollars a year, four years after arriving with no finance training and no degree. In July Cosmopolitan names him bachelor of the month, the first appearance of his face in a national magazine and the first draft of a persona he will spend three decades refining: young, unexplained, wealthy, unattached. The item runs with no account of what he does for a living. No profile published in the thirty-nine years after it supplies one either.
stops.quote: I was the only person crazy enough, or arrogant enough, or misplaced enough, to make my limit a billion dollars or more.
stops.quote_source: Vicky Ward, 'The Talented Mr. Epstein', Vanity Fair, March 2003
suggested_refs: Cosmopolitan, July 1980, 'bachelor of the month' feature

stops.name: Bear Stearns, the fifteen-thousand-dollar loan
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; the nature of the underlying conduct is disputed between sources and is not resolved here
stops.campa: An internal investigation examines a fifteen thousand dollar personal loan he has made. The firm fines him, suspends him for two months, and he resigns. Accounts of what the loan actually was differ: some describe a securities violation, others a private favour to a friend, and Bear Stearns never puts a full account on the record. He is twenty-eight, and Bear Stearns is the last firm he works for that is not his own. Within eight months he has rented an office on Central Park South and incorporated under his own name.
suggested_refs: Bear Stearns internal disciplinary practice, 1981; the firm's own silence on the reason

stops.name: Central Park South, Intercontinental Assets Group
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month for the founding; the street is attested, the suite is in no reachable record
stops.campa: He rents office space on Central Park South and incorporates Intercontinental Assets Group, describing himself as a financial consultant to the very wealthy. The clientele is thin and the room is modest. In 1984 he recovers mismanaged client money in the Cayman Islands, returns it, and becomes a millionaire on the fee. That recovery is the only piece of client business from these years that any surviving account describes in detail. He is thirty-one, and the firm has one room and no partners.
stops.quote: I want people to understand the power, the responsibility, and the burden of their money
stops.quote_source: Landon Thomas Jr., 'Jeffrey Epstein: International Moneyman of Mystery', New York Magazine, 28 October 2002
suggested_refs: Central Park South office buildings of the early 1980s; Cayman Islands fund recovery, 1984

stops.name: The Villard Houses, Towers Financial
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year of engagement; he leaves in 1989 and the collapse follows in 1993
stops.campa: Steven Hoffenberg hires him as a paid consultant to Towers Financial Corporation at twenty-five thousand dollars a month, and he works from offices in the Villard Houses, the Gilded Age mansion block beside St. Patrick's Cathedral. He leaves in 1989. Towers collapses in 1993 as the largest Ponzi scheme uncovered to that date, with losses above four hundred and fifty million dollars, and he is never charged. Hoffenberg later says Epstein ran it with him. The claim is uncorroborated and Epstein's representatives deny it.
suggested_refs: The Villard Houses, 457 Madison Avenue; the 1993 Towers Financial collapse filings

stops.name: Palm Beach, the introduction to Leslie Wexner
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; month and day not established
stops.campa: Through mutual acquaintances in Palm Beach he meets Leslie Wexner, who owns The Limited and Victoria's Secret and is among the richest men in America. Within a year he is Wexner's financial adviser. Everything that follows, the townhouse, the ranch, the aircraft, the island, the working capital, runs back through this introduction. Wexner will say in 2019 that he was defrauded of tens of millions and cut all ties around 2007. That accounting arrives only after Epstein's exposure is public, and the estate disputes it.
sources: Wexner letter to the Epstein Victims' Compensation Program, 2019
suggested_refs: Leslie Wexner and The Limited in the mid-1980s; the New Albany, Ohio, planned community

stops.name: 358 El Brillo Way, the Palm Beach house bought
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; month and day not established
stops.campa: He buys the waterfront house at 358 El Brillo Way in Palm Beach for two and a half million dollars. It is an ordinary purchase in an ordinary season, a rich man acquiring a warm-weather address a short drive from his patron's circle. Fifteen years from now this house will be the physical evidence in a criminal file: the massage table, the disconnected cameras, the list of girls' telephone numbers, the high school transcript. He owns it for twenty-nine years. It is sold in January 2021 and demolished that April.
sources: Palm Beach Police Department investigative file, 2005-2006
suggested_refs: 358 El Brillo Way as photographed before the 2021 demolition

stops.name: Columbus, the power of attorney
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month
stops.campa: Leslie Wexner grants him full power of attorney over his financial and personal affairs, the authority to sign, buy, sell, and borrow in another man's name. Three years earlier he had founded J. Epstein and Company and set its minimum client account at a billion dollars, a threshold that excludes everyone except the patron he already has. The document signed in Ohio is the actual source of the fortune. No client list of comparable size is ever produced for any other year of his life.
stops.quote: You've probably heard I'm vicious in my representation of my clients.
stops.quote_source: Vicky Ward, 'The Talented Mr. Epstein', Vanity Fair, March 2003
sources: Wexner letter to the Epstein Victims' Compensation Program, 2019
suggested_refs: The July 1991 power of attorney instrument; J. Epstein and Company's stated billion-dollar minimum

stops.name: Zorro Ranch, the high plains east of Santa Fe
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year of purchase; the property is now Rancho de San Rafael
stops.campa: He buys seven thousand six hundred acres on the high plains east of Santa Fe from former governor Bruce King for about twelve million dollars and names it Zorro Ranch: a mansion, an airstrip, a swimming pool, and rooms staff later describe as built for isolation. He tells acquaintances he intends to seed the human race with his DNA here, and floats a foundation to do it. That account comes from named associates in later reporting, never from him. New Mexico's attorney general opens an investigation into the property after his death.
stops.quote: No decorator would ever tell you to do that. But I want people to think what it means to stuff a dog.
stops.quote_source: Vicky Ward, 'The Talented Mr. Epstein', Vanity Fair, March 2003
sources: New York Times, 'Jeffrey Epstein Hoped to Seed Human Race' (2019)
New Mexico Attorney General investigation announcement, 2019
suggested_refs: Zorro Ranch airstrip and main house; the 1993 sale by former governor Bruce King

stops.name: St. Thomas, the Financial Trust Company
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; the office pin is soft, since no street address survives in any reachable source
stops.campa: He renames the firm the Financial Trust Company and moves it to St. Thomas in the U.S. Virgin Islands, where the territory's tax treatment of offshore financial services is more favorable than New York's. The money he manages, Wexner's included, now sits under Virgin Islands jurisdiction. The move is legal and ordinary. He keeps a Virgin Islands address for the rest of his life, and twenty-four years later the same territory files the civil suit against his estate that pries the structures open.
stops.quote: I like to hear voices and see faces when I interact
stops.quote_source: Landon Thomas Jr., 'Jeffrey Epstein: International Moneyman of Mystery', New York Magazine, 28 October 2002
sources: US Virgin Islands v. JEGE LLC and the Epstein estate, civil complaint, 2020
suggested_refs: Virgin Islands Economic Development Commission tax benefits; the Financial Trust Company registration

stops.name: 9 East 71st Street, the Straus house
stops.date_confidence: disputed: one Wikipedia article gives a 1995 transfer from Wexner, another a 1998 purchase for twenty million dollars paid through March 2000; the stop is placed between them and the dispute is not resolved
stops.campa: He takes possession of the Herbert N. Straus mansion at 9 East 71st Street, seven limestone storeys off Central Park and among the largest private residences in Manhattan. Sources disagree on how: one account has Wexner transferring it in 1995, another has a twenty million dollar purchase paid in instalments through March 2000. Inside, according to later testimony, there is a massage table on nearly every floor and photographs of women, some appearing to be children, displayed on the walls in the open.
stops.quote: I don't want to live in another person's house.
stops.quote_source: Landon Thomas Jr., 'Jeffrey Epstein: International Moneyman of Mystery', New York Magazine, 28 October 2002
sources: US v. Epstein, SDNY, search warrant return and bail filings, July 2019
suggested_refs: The Herbert N. Straus House facade; the July 2019 FBI search inventory

stops.name: New York, Maria Farmer goes to the FBI
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; month and day not established
stops.campa: The artist Maria Farmer reports to the FBI that Epstein has taken nude photographs of her sisters, aged twelve and sixteen. It is the first time his name reaches a federal agency in connection with a child. Nothing follows. No charge is brought and no agent returns to her. A further report goes to the Santa Monica police the following year, and a further complaint is filed in Palm Beach County in 2001. Nothing follows those either. Eight years pass between Farmer's report and the tip that opens the case that reaches a court.
suggested_refs: Maria Farmer's later public accounts of the 1996 report

stops.name: Santa Monica, the police report nobody reads
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; month and day not established
stops.campa: The model Alicia Arden files a report with the Santa Monica Police Department alleging that Epstein groped her at what had been presented to her as a Victoria's Secret audition. The brand belongs to Leslie Wexner. No charge follows. The document stays in a California police file, unread, for twenty-two years, and surfaces only in 2019 when reporters begin pulling every record with his name on it. By then the pattern the report describes has a federal indictment attached to it.
suggested_refs: Santa Monica Police Department report, 1997, as released in 2019

stops.name: Little Saint James, the island bought
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; month and day not established
stops.campa: His company L.S.J. LLC buys Little Saint James, seventy-odd acres of volcanic rock off St. Thomas, for seven million nine hundred and fifty thousand dollars. He builds a colonnaded villa, guest cabanas, a helipad, and a striped temple that carries a gold dome until Hurricane Maria tears it off in 2017. Boat crews and neighbours on St. Thomas call the place Orgy Island and Pedophile Island years before any conviction. Multiple accusers, Virginia Giuffre among them, testify to being trafficked here.
sources: Court testimony, Giuffre v. Maxwell, SDNY
suggested_refs: The striped temple building on Little Saint James, dome intact and dome gone

stops.name: West Palm Beach, the students of Palm Beach Atlantic
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; the file is closed in 2004
stops.campa: Three female students at Palm Beach Atlantic University report that Ghislaine Maxwell recruited them for Epstein. A file is opened. It is closed in 2004 without a charge, three years later and seven months before the Palm Beach police receive the tip that starts the case that sticks. Maxwell will be convicted in 2021 as his co-conspirator in trafficking, on conduct that includes the recruitment this file describes. The 2001 file and the 2005 investigation that convicts him belong to the same county, four years apart.
suggested_refs: Palm Beach Atlantic University, 2001; the 2004 closure of the file

stops.name: The MIT Media Lab, the gifts logged as anonymous
stops.date_confidence: attested as a span, roughly 2002 to 2017; the stop is placed at the opening of the span
stops.campa: MIT's own outside-counsel review will find roughly eight hundred and fifty thousand dollars given to the university across a decade and a half, about five hundred and twenty-five thousand of it to the Media Lab, logged internally as anonymous to conceal that the donor is a registered sex offender. He visits the campus after his 2008 conviction. Director Joi Ito resigns in September 2019 when Ronan Farrow publishes the concealment. The review that establishes the figures is published in 2020, the year after the donor is dead.
stops.quote: I invest in people—be it politics or science. It's what I do.
stops.quote_source: Landon Thomas Jr., 'Jeffrey Epstein: International Moneyman of Mystery', New York Magazine, 28 October 2002 (said to friends; Epstein granted no interview)
suggested_refs: The MIT Media Lab building; the 2020 Goodwin Procter report on the gifts

stops.name: Paris, the apartment on Avenue Foch
stops.date_confidence: attested as a span across the 2000s; the pin is the atlas's canonical Paris pin rather than the Avenue Foch address
stops.campa: He keeps an apartment on Avenue Foch, the widest boulevard in Paris, running from the Arc de Triomphe down to the Bois de Boulogne. It serves as the European base. French prosecutors open an investigation after his death into possible trafficking of minors in France between 1999 and 2015 connected to this address, and the modelling agent Jean-Luc Brunel, tied to him for decades, is arrested in 2020 on allegations rooted in the same operation. The Paris file is opened only once the man it concerns is dead.
sources: French National Financial Prosecutor's Office investigation announcement, 2019
Le Monde and Reuters reporting on the Jean-Luc Brunel arrest, 2020
suggested_refs: Avenue Foch, 16th arrondissement; the PNF investigation opened in 2019

stops.name: Dakar, the aircraft on the Africa trip
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the trip is attested but which legs were flown on Epstein's aircraft is reported inconsistently and is not resolved here
stops.campa: Bill Clinton crosses Africa in September examining AIDS programs, travelling with Kevin Spacey and Chris Tucker, and flight logs later published indicate that aircraft owned by Epstein carried at least part of the itinerary. Which legs is reported inconsistently: some accounts list Senegal, others emphasize different stops, and Clinton's staff say he flew a handful of times with Secret Service throughout. The trip becomes one of the recurring exhibits in the flight-log record that follows Epstein for the rest of his life.
stops.quote: If you were a boxer at the downtown gymnasium at 14th Street and Mike Tyson walked in, your face would have the same look as these foreign leaders had when Clinton entered the room. He is the world's greatest politician.
stops.quote_source: Landon Thomas Jr., 'Jeffrey Epstein: International Moneyman of Mystery', New York Magazine, 28 October 2002
sources: Flight logs published by Fox News and Gawker, 2016
Clinton Foundation trip itinerary (contradicts the logs in detail)
suggested_refs: The 2002 Clinton Africa itinerary; the unsealed Epstein flight manifests

stops.name: New York, the moneyman profiled
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day of publication
stops.campa: Landon Thomas Jr. publishes a profile in New York Magazine that gives him his lasting epithet, the international moneyman of mystery, and prints the sentences he wants printed. He grants no interview; the best lines are relayed by friends. Donald Trump speaks to the reporter on a speakerphone and says Epstein likes beautiful women as much as he does, many of them on the younger side. Everyone in the piece is on the record.
stops.quote: I've known Jeff for fifteen years. Terrific guy. He's a lot of fun to be with. It is even said that he likes beautiful women as much as I do, and many of them are on the younger side. No doubt about it—Jeffrey enjoys his social life.
stops.quote_source: Donald Trump, quoted in Landon Thomas Jr., New York Magazine, 28 October 2002 (the original splits the quotation with an attribution clause)
sources: Landon Thomas Jr., New York Magazine, 28 October 2002
suggested_refs: New York Magazine, 28 October 2002 cover and profile spread

stops.name: Harvard, the Program for Evolutionary Dynamics
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year of the gift; the office access continues past 2008
stops.campa: He gives Harvard six and a half million dollars, funding the Program for Evolutionary Dynamics under Martin Nowak, and receives in exchange an office on campus. He hosts scientists there and cultivates faculty. By the university's own later account he keeps using the office after his 2008 conviction and his registration as a sex offender. Harvard announces in 2020 that it will not return the gift and redirects remaining Epstein-linked funds to survivor support and prevention research.
sources: Harvard University public statement and report on Epstein donations, 2020
suggested_refs: The Program for Evolutionary Dynamics; Harvard's 2020 report on the donations

stops.name: New York, the Vanity Fair profile
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month of publication
stops.campa: Vicky Ward publishes The Talented Mr. Epstein in Vanity Fair. He opens their interview by putting a chessboard between them and giving her white. He explains the taxidermy in his townhouse by saying he wants people to think about what it means to stuff a dog, and tells her he is there to represent his client even against the client's own family. It is the fullest account of him published in his lifetime. It contains no allegation of a crime, and none of the three police reports already filed against him appears in it.
stops.quote: Let's play chess. You be white. You get the first move.
stops.quote_source: Vicky Ward, 'The Talented Mr. Epstein', Vanity Fair, March 2003
sources: Vicky Ward, 'The Talented Mr. Epstein', Vanity Fair, March 2003
suggested_refs: Vanity Fair, March 2003; the townhouse interiors described in the piece

stops.name: Palm Beach International Airport, the logs
stops.date_confidence: attested as a span across the 1990s and 2000s; the stop is placed at the opening of the criminal period
stops.campa: His aircraft, including the Boeing 727 the tabloids call the Lolita Express, work out of Palm Beach International, moving him and his guests between the mansion, the island, and Europe. The logs kept by his pilots list passengers by name, flight after flight, for more than a decade. Subpoenaed in civil litigation and unsealed in 2019 and 2020, they become the single most quoted document of the case. The airport itself is an ordinary regional field with a general aviation ramp, and no source places a criminal act on its grounds.
sources: Epstein flight logs, released in Giuffre v. Maxwell, SDNY, unsealed 2019-2020
suggested_refs: The unsealed flight manifests; the Boeing 727 registered to Epstein

stops.name: Palm Beach, the tip and the donation
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month for the tip; the ninety thousand dollar donation is attested to 14 December 2004
stops.campa: In November the Palm Beach police receive a tip from a family about a young woman found at Epstein's house, and the investigation that becomes the first criminal case against him opens. On the fourteenth of December, with detectives already working, he donates ninety thousand dollars to the Palm Beach Police Department. The department takes the money and keeps working. Its detectives will spend thirteen months on the file that the donation did not close, and hand it to prosecutors who narrow it to one count.
sources: Palm Beach Police Department investigative file, 2005-2006
suggested_refs: The 14 December 2004 donation record; the Palm Beach Police Department under Chief Michael Reiter

stops.name: Palm Beach, the fourteen-year-old and three hundred dollars
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month
stops.campa: A woman reports to the police that her fourteen-year-old stepdaughter was paid three hundred dollars to strip and massage Epstein at the Palm Beach house. The sum recurs across the statements detectives take: three hundred dollars, cash, per visit, with a further payment for bringing another girl. The recruitment is done by the girls themselves, which is how the number of them grows the way it does. Detectives will identify approximately thirty-five of them inside the next fourteen months.
sources: Palm Beach Police Department investigative file, 2005-2006
suggested_refs: Palm Beach police witness statements, March 2005

stops.name: 358 El Brillo Way, the search
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month
stops.campa: Palm Beach police execute a search warrant at 358 El Brillo Way. They find surveillance cameras disconnected before their arrival, photographs of nude and partially nude young women throughout the house, books on sadomasochism, and a high school transcript belonging to one of the girls in the file. Detective Joseph Recarey's report catalogues the rooms. The evidence is exactly the evidence that the state's eventual single charge of solicitation will not describe.
sources: Palm Beach Police Department investigative file, 2005-2006
suggested_refs: The October 2005 search warrant return; Detective Joseph Recarey's case file

stops.name: Palm Beach, thirty-five girls and the affidavit
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month for the affidavit; the thirteen-month investigation spans 2005 and 2006
stops.campa: The police conclude a thirteen-month investigation identifying approximately thirty-five girls under the age of consent who had contact with Epstein at the Palm Beach house, and file a probable cause affidavit charging four counts of unlawful sex with minors and one count of sexual abuse. The affidavit goes to the state attorney's office. What comes back from the grand jury in July is one count of felony solicitation of prostitution, a charge whose wording turns the children in the file into prostitutes.
sources: Palm Beach Police Department investigative file, 2005-2006
suggested_refs: The May 2006 probable cause affidavit; the July 2006 grand jury return

stops.name: West Palm Beach, one count
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day of arrest
stops.campa: He is arrested on the single state solicitation charge and pleads not guilty. The same month the FBI opens its own inquiry under the name Operation Leap Year, the federal government having concluded that the state charge does not describe what happened. Two investigations now run in parallel on the same conduct, a Florida prostitution case and a federal sex trafficking case. Only one of them will ever be filed, and it will not be the federal one.
suggested_refs: The July 2006 state arrest record; the FBI's Operation Leap Year

stops.name: Miami, sixty counts drafted
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month of drafting
stops.campa: Assistant United States Attorney Marie Villafana drafts a fifty-three page federal indictment carrying sixty counts. It names the conduct plainly and it is ready to file. The office belongs to United States Attorney Alexander Acosta, who does not file it. The document exists, complete, in the Southern District of Florida in the summer of 2007, and it is never filed. No grand jury ever sees it. Acosta enters plea discussions the following August, is confirmed Secretary of Labor in 2017, and resigns in July 2019.
suggested_refs: The unfiled 53-page indictment of June 2007; AUSA Marie Villafana's role

stops.name: Miami, the non-prosecution agreement
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day of signing
stops.campa: A non-prosecution agreement is signed granting Epstein immunity from federal sex trafficking charges. Acosta had entered plea discussions the month before. The sixty-count indictment is never filed and the federal case ends without a courtroom, replaced by a state proceeding whose single charge carries a sentence measured in months. The agreement stays out of public view for a decade. When it surfaces, in the Miami Herald in 2018, it costs the sitting Secretary of Labor his job within eight months.
suggested_refs: The 24 September 2007 non-prosecution agreement; Acosta's July 2019 resignation

stops.name: West Palm Beach, the plea
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: He pleads guilty in Florida state court to one count of solicitation of prostitution and one count of solicitation of a minor under eighteen. He is sentenced to eighteen months and ordered to register as a sex offender. Thirty-five girls are in the police file. Two counts are in the judgment. The registration is public from this date forward. Harvard lets him keep his campus office afterwards and MIT keeps taking his money, logging it as anonymous.
suggested_refs: The 30 June 2008 Florida state judgment; the sex offender registration record

stops.name: Palm Beach County Stockade, the sentence begins
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month; the pin resolves the Gun Club Road jail corridor rather than the Stockade building itself
stops.campa: He serves the sentence at the Palm Beach County Stockade on the Gun Club Road corridor, a minimum security county facility rather than a state prison. He is housed away from the general population. Sheriff's deputies later describe an arrangement lax even by the standards of county work release. Of the eighteen months imposed he will serve about thirteen. The Miami Herald obtains the sheriff's records a decade later, and the arrangement they describe is the reason the sentence is reported at all.
suggested_refs: The Palm Beach County jail complex on Gun Club Road; deputies' work-release testimony

stops.name: West Palm Beach, the office of the foundation
stops.date_confidence: attested as beginning roughly three and a half months into the sentence, so about mid-October 2008; the pool's August date is wrong
stops.campa: About three and a half months into the sentence he is granted work release: up to twelve hours a day, six days a week, at an office he rents in West Palm Beach for a foundation with a scientific sounding name, driven there and back by a sheriff's deputy who logs the trips. Investigative reporting later establishes a stream of visitors during those hours. He is released outright in 2009 after about thirteen months. What the office was actually for, beyond receiving people, the surviving logs do not say.
sources: Miami Herald, 'Perversion of Justice' (Julie K. Brown, 2018)
suggested_refs: Sheriff's work-release transport logs, 2008-2009; the Florida Science Foundation office

stops.name: Great Saint James, the second island
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; month and day not established
stops.campa: He buys the neighbouring island of Great Saint James, one hundred and sixty-five acres, for twenty-two and a half million dollars, doubling the private archipelago. Construction begins. The Virgin Islands government later sues the estate over unpermitted building that damaged the shoreline and the reef. The purchase is made eight years after his conviction and registration as a sex offender, by a man whose Florida sentence is a matter of public record, with money nobody has yet been able to fully account for.
stops.quote: Very few people need any more money when they have a billion dollars. The key is not to have it do harm more than anything else…. You don't want to lose your money.
stops.quote_source: Vicky Ward, 'The Talented Mr. Epstein', Vanity Fair, March 2003
sources: US Virgin Islands v. Epstein estate, civil complaint, 2020
suggested_refs: Great Saint James construction as documented in the USVI complaint

stops.name: Miami, Perversion of Justice
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month of publication of the series
stops.campa: Julie K. Brown publishes Perversion of Justice in the Miami Herald, a series built on the Palm Beach police file, the sealed federal agreement, and the survivors who agree to be named. It establishes what the non-prosecution agreement did and who signed it. Within eight months Acosta has resigned as Secretary of Labor and the Southern District of New York has opened the case that the Southern District of Florida closed in 2007. The reporting is the mechanism. Nothing else moved for eleven years.
stops.quote: He's charming. In a devious way, he's charming. To some extent it's a typical tragedy where he believes his own bullshit.
stops.quote_source: Jeffrey Epstein on Donald Trump, interviewed on audio tape by Michael Wolff, 2017; excerpts released November 2024 and lodged in the U.S. House document repository, 27 February 2025
sources: Miami Herald, 'Perversion of Justice' (Julie K. Brown, 2018)
Julie K. Brown, Perversion of Justice, HarperCollins, 2021
suggested_refs: The Miami Herald series, November 2018; the survivors who went on the record

stops.name: Teterboro, the plane from Paris
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: His aircraft lands at Teterboro from Paris and federal agents are waiting on the tarmac. He is arrested on charges of sex trafficking of minors and conspiracy, alleged to have occurred between 2002 and 2005, the same years the Palm Beach file already covered. Teterboro has been his northeastern hub for twenty years, the field his logs name more than any other. He is taken from the bottom of the aircraft stairs to a cell in Manhattan, and he does not leave federal custody again.
sources: US v. Epstein, SDNY criminal complaint and arrest documentation, July 2019
suggested_refs: Teterboro Airport general aviation ramp; the July 2019 arrest documentation

stops.name: 9 East 71st Street, the safe
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the search runs through the night into 7 July
stops.campa: Agents execute a warrant on the townhouse the same night and work through into the next day. They open a safe and find cash, loose diamonds, and an expired Austrian passport bearing his photograph under a different name and a Saudi Arabian address. There are CDs labelled with women's names and photographs displayed openly on the walls. Prosecutors put the passport in front of the court at the bail hearing as the measure of what this defendant can do if he is allowed outside the building.
sources: FBI search warrant return and court filings, US v. Epstein bail hearing, SDNY, July 2019
suggested_refs: The July 2019 search warrant return inventory; the expired Austrian passport exhibit

stops.name: Manhattan, the federal courthouse
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day of arraignment; bail is denied on 18 July, not 18 August as the pool had it
stops.campa: He is arraigned in the Southern District of New York before Judge Richard Berman and pleads not guilty. Bail is denied on the eighteenth, the court citing flight risk. The same courthouse has taken in other men whose fortunes were assembled offshore, financiers indicted decades apart with nothing but the address in common. This one it will not get to try; the case is dismissed on the twenty-ninth of August, weeks after Epstein is found dead in his cell.
suggested_refs: The Daniel Patrick Moynihan United States Courthouse, 500 Pearl Street

stops.name: The Metropolitan Correctional Center, the cell on Park Row
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day of death; the medical examiner's ruling is dated 16 August and is disputed by the family
stops.campa: He is held at the Metropolitan Correctional Center on Park Row, beside the courthouse. On the twenty-third of July he is found injured in his cell under circumstances never established. On the tenth of August he is found dead. The cellmate had been moved out days earlier and the two assigned guards later admit falsifying their observation logs. The chief medical examiner rules suicide by hanging on the sixteenth. His family and the pathologist Michael Baden dispute the ruling. The facility closes for good in 2021.
sources: NYC Office of Chief Medical Examiner ruling, 2019
DOJ Office of Inspector General report on MCC failures, 2023
suggested_refs: MCC New York, 150 Park Row, before its 2021 closure; the DOJ Inspector General findings

stops.name: Star of David, the unmarked tomb
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the pool's August date and its coordinates were both wrong
stops.campa: He is buried in an unmarked tomb beside his parents at the IJ Morris Star of David mausoleum in Palm Beach County, twenty-five kilometres from the house on El Brillo Way. The estate is valued at roughly six hundred million dollars. There is no plaque, no inscription, no name on the stone. The iconography survives instead in the booking photograph, the flight logs, the black book, and a sentence the internet writes within days of the death and has not stopped writing since.
sources: Palm Beach Post reporting on the burial, 2019
Washington Post, 'The internet has decided Jeffrey Epstein didn't kill himself', August 2019
suggested_refs: The IJ Morris Star of David mausoleum, 9321 Memorial Park Road; the 2008 Palm Beach County booking photograph
